subject: Prompt-set regression: mitigation proposal & short A/B guardrail plan
thread_content:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Willow Analytics (procurement@willow.ai)
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Prompt-set regression: mitigation proposal & short A/B guardrail plan

Team — quick sync request. After last night's scheduled prompt-suite rollout for Acme Corp we saw an unexpected drop in our "helpful_rate" on a small but high-value percent of traffic (roughly 2.8% delta on the control window). The customer flagged several hallucination examples; I attached the raw eval results.

I want us to converge on: (1) a short mitigation that we can ship in the next 48–72 hours if needed, (2) a conservative A/B plan for the patch that preserves our latency SLO, and (3) clear acceptance criteria so we can either promote or rollback cleanly.

What I'm proposing in this first pass (open to feedback):
- Hotfix prompt revert to previous prompt template (v1.4) as a fallback route.
- Run a 10% canary for 72 hours vs baseline, with these primary signals: helpful_rate, hallucination_rate, and median p95 latency.
- Acceptance: helpful_rate delta <= 0.5% vs baseline AND hallucination_rate reduction >= 40% on flagged signal set.

Attachments: eval_results_v2.csv (filtered examples + metric sinks).

Can each of you call out risks / infra constraints / test coverage gaps? I'll schedule a 30-min sync if we need live triage.

— Rishi

-----------------------------------------------
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt-set regression: mitigation proposal & short A/B guardrail plan

Thanks Rishi — looked through the CSV and a few patterns stand out (system prompt drift + one prompt variant amplified a low-quality decode path). My read: revert to v1.4 as you suggested is sensible as a short-term mitigation.

Proposed A/B plan (quick draft, will put a doc in Drive):
- Variant A: baseline (current live prompt).
- Variant B: v1.4 with a small normalization tweak (trim repeated tokens, add explicit no-hallucination instruction).
- Traffic split: 90% baseline / 10% variant B for 72 hours. If variant B meets acceptance, expand to 50/50 for another 48 hours before promoting.
- Primary metrics: helpful_rate (core), hallucination_rate (manual-labeled sample), median p95 latency. Secondary: token_cost_delta, user-drop-rate.

I attached ab_plan_draft.md. Two asks for Product: confirm the rollback trigger for user-impacting complaints (I suggest immediate rollback if user-drop-rate > 1% absolute increase).

— Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prompt-set regression: mitigation proposal & short A/B guardrail plan

Quick infra notes:
- We can deploy v1.4 fallback and route for a 10% canary within 4–6 hours; need a short maintenance window to warm caches and KV prefixes.
- p95 latency may vary slightly due to cache warming; recommend a 12-hour warmup before we start collecting canary stats.
- Autoscaling: we'll pin a dedicated pool for the canary to avoid noisy neighbor effects (small cost impact).

I'll include a Canary config snippet in the Drive doc and open INF-1428 for rollout automation (linked). Also flagged: logging/trace hooks need to capture prompt-template-id in the token traces so QA can slice by variant.

— Dev

-----------------------------------------------
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prompt-set regression: mitigation proposal & short A/B guardrail plan

QA can turn around manual labeling for the flagged sample set in ~24 hours if we get the final sample list. A couple of important notes from the test plan:
- We'll run both automated unit checks and a manual triage of 500 examples (stratified) for hallucination labels. Manual labels will be the source of truth for hallucination_rate.
- Metric matrix attached (metric_matrix.xlsx) lists exact calculation formulas and the SQL queries for the dashboards.
- We need the prompt-template-id in the trace logs (per Dev) so we can slice by variant. Without it, the manual labels won't align with telemetry.

Attachment: metric_matrix.xlsx (metric definitions + queries).

— Laura

-----------------------------------------------
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prompt-set regression: mitigation proposal & short A/B guardrail plan

Thanks all — a few product/governance points to close before we act:
1) Acceptance criteria refinement — make thresholds explicit in the runbook:
   - helpful_rate delta: <= +0.5% (no degradation).
   - hallucination_rate: >= 40% relative improvement on stratified sample.
   - p95 latency: no more than +75ms absolute versus baseline during steady-state (post-warmup).
   - user-drop-rate: must not increase > 0.5% absolute during canary.
2) Manual escalation path — if we see borderline improvement (e.g., hallucination improves 30–39%), we hold and create a Priority-1 postmortem-runbook and widen manual review.
3) Communication — we'll notify Acme's contact (J. Smith) that we're running a conservative canary and provide daily summary with annotated examples.

I'll update the Drive doc with the acceptance matrix and the decision tree (promote / hold / rollback).

— Tessa

-----------------------------------------------
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prompt-set regression: mitigation proposal & short A/B guardrail plan

Appreciate the quick replies and clear asks. Summary / decisions: 
- Action: deploy v1.4 fallback tonight to standby (no traffic) and prepare canary config.
- Canary: 10% traffic for 72 hours after a 12-hour warmup window.
- Acceptance (finalized): helpful_rate delta <= 0.5% vs baseline; hallucination_rate >= 40% relative improvement on the stratified sample; p95 latency <= +75ms post-warmup; user-drop-rate <= +0.5% absolute.
- Rollback trigger: user-drop-rate > 1% absolute at any time during canary OR any verified P0 hallucination that affects an SLA customer flow. Immediate rollback if either occurs.
- Owners: Marissa (experiment owner), Dev (rollout infra), Laura (manual labeling), Tessa & Rishi (product decision sign-off).

Next steps: Marissa, please finalize the A/B doc in Drive and ping Procurement to let Acme know (cc Willow Analytics as FYI). Dev, open INF-1428 and post the canary snippet. Laura, send the 500-sample list and start the labeling once traces are available.

I'll run a 15-min stand-up at 09:30 if anyone wants to jump on.

— Rishi
